text: Disputed: whether the round-3 review still has a C list to answer, after the lane held worker/T-0317 BACK 'kind=review' three times running. Checked directly: none of the three reviews (1/2/3-t-0317.md) has a `## C` heading or any C-list content — `asf.evidence.review.c_items()` returns `[]` for all three, and each says in prose "No C list — nothing found that blocks." The hold is a false positive of the lane's own tooling: `asf.reviews.verdict()` (asf/reviews.py:150-158) derives BOUNCE (read as CHANGES by asf/evidence/review.py) because its `missing()` check requires an exact normalized-string match between the table's row names and `CHECKLIST['code']`'s literal text, and the rows all three reviewers wrote ("scope: the diff stays inside `writes:`", "acceptance tests byte-identical to the plan's") are exactly what `asf/briefs/templates/review.md:10-15` itself instructs every reviewer to write — a drift between the checklist (added by T-0265/#135) and the template that was never reconciled. Rounds 1-2 additionally hit a hard table-parse fault from an unescaped `|` inside one evidence cell's grep pattern. This is not specific to T-0317: the same table wording bounces docs/reviews/1-b-0087.md, 1-b-0090.md, 1-b-0099.md and 1-b-0110.md identically. Overruled: there is no C list and no code defect — the diff, the tests, and the gate are exactly what three independent rounds each verified and approved; T-0317's footprint and content stand unchanged. Separately, round 2's carried-forward I-item (write_agents_file's `tools=()` rendering `"tools": []`, spec §2.1 vs §2.4's worked example) is also not a Task-1 defect — T4's acceptance text (docs/specs/f-0062.md:746) literally reads "tools is the row's set minus deny_tools", and asf/roles/launch.py:144 implements that formula exactly — but it stays open, unresolved, for whoever wires Task 4/5's launch to confirm the rendered agents file is read the way the runtime expects.

Three prior sessions left `plan/F-0067` empty — no `docs/plans/f-0067.md`, no `docs/reviews/1-f-0067.md`, no Task cards anywhere in the repo's history. This was a starved plan, not a content dispute: there were no two readings to weigh, only nothing committed after three attempts. I read the approved spec in full and verified every precondition its §1.1 states against this checkout (`step_health.run()`'s statement order, `worktrees.safety`'s two `unpushed commit(s)` exits, `retention.owned_patterns`, `doctor.run`'s row order, `groom`'s `EXTRA_SECTIONS`, `plugin_build`'s skill list) — all matched exactly, so the spec itself was never the obstacle. `docs/plans/f-0066.md` (landed since, at `eac200f76`) gave the precedent for how this factory plans a tightly-coupled single-new-module feature, and `T-0317`'s ruling (`111165f56`) gave the precedent for not forcing a split where one does not exist. So I wrote and landed the missing plan myself rather than ordering a fourth attempt: five Tasks — `conventions.py`'s `floor:` map (no dependency), the whole of `asf/floor.py` plus its two satellite files `retention.py`/`worktrees.py` (one Task: the registry, probes, sweep and hold branch all share one new file and one test module, and `CLASSES`' own `FloorError` check at import means a partial table fails its own registry test — it does not split), then three independent callers (doctor row, groom section, tick+CLI wiring) that each need only the leaf. Verified against the live parser: `plan_task_records`/`writes_lines`/`task_order` read the five headings, their `writes:` and `after:` lines exactly as intended (`{1: [], 2: [1], 3: [2], 4: [2], 5: [2]}`), so Task cards will mint correctly once this plan lands on `main`. One standing, already-repeatedly-recorded defect noted in the plan itself (PD8) and not fixed here, out of this Feature's footprint: `plan_tasks.STORY_ID_RE` is four digits and the spec's Story ids are five, so the minted Task cards' `stories:` field will read empty — the same defect a dozen other landed plans in this repo have already recorded at this head. Nothing else was in dispute; the card's own "fold into the clean-floor Feature?" question was already answered by the spec itself (§1.3: stands alone either way) and is not reopened.
